findings.failure_mode: Log searches over large or busy tenants repeatedly return empty pages with a 'timed out' progress flag, so the user watches the search crawl through slices without results. Other ClickHouse resource-limit errors surface as a hard error banner.
findings.trigger_condition: A search with a rare or non-word term, or a wide time range on a high-volume environment, exceeds the 8s (first slice) or 5s (later slices) max_execution_time.
findings.amplifier: Each timeout is turned into a retry slice (retryTimedOutLogsSearchSlice) and handed back as a cursor, so the caller re-issues the next query. Nothing in this path counts per-tenant timeouts or backs off, and the slice query is the same expensive scan that just timed out.
findings.sustaining_effect: Every timed-out request returns a next cursor, so a client that auto-continues keeps issuing 5-8s scans against the shared ClickHouse. There is no breaker or budget, so the load persists until the slice ladder is exhausted or the user leaves.
findings.blast_radius: ClickHouse capacity for the logs list queries is consumed. Other log viewers and query users on the same cluster may see slower or timed-out searches.

evidence.note: Timeout is converted into a retry slice and a cursor, with no backoff or budget.
Only an abort signal is passed; the server-side max_execution_time is the sole bound.
Earlier [fix] to bound logs search memory and pagination at scale; the same cost problem is still being tuned.
Latest change added adaptive time slices, which is where the timeout retry loop comes from.

findings.confidence_rationale: I did not see the client or route code that decides whether to auto-continue after a timed-out slice, and the retry-slice helper is in another file I did not open. The risk rests on this presenter's logic alone.
findings.how_to_verify: Search a high-volume environment for a non-word term over a long period. Check whether the route or UI follows the returned cursor automatically, and count the ClickHouse queries tagged log_comment 'logs_list' per user action.
findings.prediction: Further perf or fix commits to this file will tune slice sizes or time limits for large tenants.
